title: Four-Table JOIN with Category Filter
description:
Join orders, customers, products, and categories to produce a filtered report showing only **completed** orders for **Electronics** products.

**Tables:** `categories(id, name)`, `products(id, name, category_id)`, `customers(id, name)`, `orders(id, customer_id, product_id, status, amount)`

Output columns: `order_id`, `customer_name`, `product_name`, `status`, `amount`. Order by `order_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE categories (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO categories VALUES (1,'Electronics'),(2,'Clothing'),(3,'Books'); CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category_id INT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A',1),(2,'Shirt X',2),(3,'Book 1',3),(4,'Gadget Y',1),(5,'Laptop Z',1); CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'),(3,'Carol'),(4,'Dave'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, product_id INT, status VARCHAR, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,1,'completed',49.99),(2,1,2,'completed',29.99),(3,2,4,'completed',79.99),(4,2,3,'pending',14.99),(5,3,5,'completed',999.99),(6,3,1,'cancelled',49.99),(7,4,4,'completed',79.99),(8,4,2,'completed',29.99);
solution_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name, o.status, o.amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND cat.name = 'Electronics' ORDER BY o.id

test_cases.description: Completed Electronics orders: ids 1 (Widget A), 3 (Gadget Y), 5 (Laptop Z), 7 (Gadget Y) — 4 rows

hints: Chain the four JOINs: orders → customers, orders → products, products → categories.
Apply WHERE filters AFTER all joins; filter by status = 'completed' AND category name = 'Electronics'.
explanation: The four-table join links orders to customers (for names), to products (for product names), and products to categories (for category filtering). WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND cat.name = 'Electronics' keeps only Electronics orders that were completed. Orders 2 (Clothing), 4 (pending), 6 (cancelled), 8 (Clothing) are excluded. 4 rows remain.
